title: refactor(ci): consolidate lint/test workflows, upgrade GH actions and deps, release automation hygiene
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: our GitHub Actions surface area has drifted into several repository-specific and legacy workflows which increases maintenance burden, slows CI iteration, and makes release automation flaky. This PR consolidates lint/test/release pipelines into a smaller set of reusable workflows, upgrades GH Actions and common action versions, bumps Node versions where needed, and performs dependency hygiene for CI-related packages.

Summary of changes: consolidated multiple per-repo workflows into .github/workflows/ci.yml and moved reusable job definitions to .github/workflows/reusable/*.yml; upgraded actions/checkout, setup-node, cache actions to latest stable releases; bumped CI Node version matrix to 18 and 20 where packages support it; added more aggressive caching for npm and poetry; fixed a flaky integration test by increasing DB setup timeout and adding retry logic to the migration script; disabled a deprecated release workflow and replaced it with an opt-in reusable release workflow that requires a release label.

Checklist:
- [x] Consolidate lint/test jobs into single workflow with job-level caching and concurrency groups
- [x] Upgrade GH Actions used in CI to latest supported versions
- [x] Reduce matrix size for non-critical integration tests to improve runtime cost
- [x] Add opt-in release automation reusable workflow and document usage in CONTRIBUTING.md
- [x] Run full CI across redwood monorepo and fix failing test flakes
- [x] Add release notes describing operational impact

Impact and rationale: consolidating the workflows reduces duplication and makes it easier to add cross-repo improvements (caching, shared secrets, SLS alerts). Upgrading actions addresses several flaky issues and removes noisy deprecation logs from Actions runner. The new release automation requires explicit label gating which reduces accidental releases from automated runs. Cost: this reduces duplicated work in parallel CI runs and should slightly reduce total CI minutes across active repos after rollout.

Rollout plan: landed as a merged PR to main. Re-enabled workflows in dependent repos incrementally by switching their calls to the reusable jobs. Communications posted to #infra and a short doc section added to CONTRIBUTING.md on how to consume the reusable workflows.

Notes: the initial CI run failed due to a missing NODE_AUTH_TOKEN for a private package; fixed by moving npm setup to a dedicated step that only runs when AUTH is present. All subsequent CI runs are green.
